label: rem:topological-vs-pl-link-type
title: Topological links and polygonal link types
html:
A topological link enters this paper only through a polygonal representative, and such links are tame. The link type of a polygonal link is a PL notion. Its relation to topological ambient isotopy has two parts.

  1. Smooth isotopies. If two polygonal links are joined by a C^1 ambient isotopy, they have the same link type. Sampling each component finely enough keeps the inscribed polygons simple and disjoint along the isotopy, yielding a sequence of elementary \Delta-moves.

  2. Topological isotopies. A topological ambient isotopy cannot in general be replaced by a C^1 one, because a C^1 diffeomorphism cannot carry the carrier of a triangle onto the carrier of a square. In dimension three, topologically ambient isotopic tame links are PL ambient isotopic. This follows from Moise's triangulation theorem and Bing's tameness theorem [moise1952, bing1954]. Here this comparison is cited from the three-manifold literature rather than proved from scratch, so equality of link types for topologically isotopic links is conditional on the Moise–Bing theorem.

  3. The ambient space. The definition is stated in a real inner-product space V, while the Alexander--Markov remarks place links in S^3. For \dim V = 3 the two settings give the same link types. A compact link in S^3 = \mathbb{R}^3 \cup \{\infty\} misses a point, and an ambient isotopy of S^3 can be adjusted to fix a point off the link, so the classification of tame links up to ambient isotopy is the same in \mathbb{R}^3 and in S^3 [rolfsen, lickorish1997]. The cited Moise--Bing comparison likewise concerns \dim V = 3; only the three-dimensional case is supported by the classical triangulation theorems.

The link type defined here is distinct from the two-element type of braid link types, which enumerates only the unknot and the Hopf link.
